answer:
**Regression testing needs representative requests, explicit expectations, and a stable comparison.** Build a versioned replay set covering ordinary tasks and important failure slices. Pin model, prompt, tool, and data versions, then compare baseline and candidate quality, schemas, latency, resource cost, and errors. [1](https://research.google/pubs/the-ml-test-score-a-rubric-for-ml-production-readiness-and-technical-debt-reduction/)

Some expectations can be exact, such as valid schema or arithmetic. Others require source-grounded judgments or human review. Define thresholds and uncertainty handling rather than treating every small automated-score change as decisive.

**Shadowing must isolate side effects.** Duplicate permitted live inputs to a candidate whose outputs are not sent to users and whose external writes are disabled or simulated. Protect sensitive data and avoid consuming production capacity unpredictably.

Include cold starts, cache differences, timeouts, and dependency failures. Replay and shadowing can establish regression and operational evidence, but neither measures users' causal response to unseen outputs. Follow with an appropriate online experiment when behavior changes matter. The test system should verify the deployed workflow, not only a clean model call in isolation.

**Technical details and references.**

Build a versioned replay set of representative requests with expected schemas, reference labels/evidence where available, and important failure slices. Run baseline and candidate under pinned model/configuration/data versions, measuring quality, schema validity, latency, token/resource cost, and error rates. Gate merges on explicit thresholds and uncertainty, allowing human review for ambiguous quality changes. [1](https://research.google/pubs/the-ml-test-score-a-rubric-for-ml-production-readiness-and-technical-debt-reduction/)

For shadowing, duplicate permitted live inputs to an isolated candidate whose outputs and side effects are not delivered to users. Disable external writes and use controlled tool responses. Protect sensitive data with approved retention/redaction, and separate replay traffic from production capacity. Include cold starts, cache states, timeouts, and dependency failures. Offline replay and shadowing establish regression evidence, but cannot replace randomized online measurement of changed user behavior.
